newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run offered at strong price.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run offered at strong price.

text.p: Scarcer European low sulphur straight-run continued to be offered at a strong prices on Thursday, but a potential buyer for a prompt cargo was shying away due to a problem over loading.

A Norwegian major was still asking $103 fob for his July 5-10 loader but no deals were heard despite reports that a U.S. refiner was eyeing the 25,000 tonne cargo to top up three other cargoes picked up recently at cheaper prices.

"I think the (U.S. refiner) needs a top-up but the loading date is too soon. If the seller can get a delay of two to three days they may have a deal otherwise they would be looking for alternatives," one trader said.

A second trader seconded the view that the problem barring the deal was operational, not disagreement over the price, adding he did not see the seller going lower as it has the option of taking it into their own system.

"They've been at $103 since Day 1 and I don't see them backing down...They may have their own value attached to the straight-run and it may be more worthwhile for them to take it in themselves," she added.

The first trader, with a U.K.-based major, said he was not interested in the cargo due to the higher price. Three deals were concluded since last Friday at prices between $98 and $100.75 fob, all by the U.S. buyer.
High sulphur straight-run was largely steady, after one Russian M-100 was reported traded at two means +$2/$4, the range the seller was asking for on Wednesday.
"There seems to be a bit of scarcity in straight-run at the moment," a trader with a major said.
A second European trader said it sold late on Wednesday a 30,000-tonne cargo of high sulphur straight-run out of Mercin loading July 10-12, but the price was private and confidential.
